- If sentiment is positive (≥0.2) in the last 24 days, model tends to under-forecast; adjust forecast upward by 1–3% of recent mean or 2–5 points depending on volatility.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no spike, but true outcome has sharp spike later, model is lagging; add 2–5 points to forecast at spike window (e.g., 10–15 days ahead).
- After a true price spike (e.g., >90), model often overshoots in next 5–7 days; cap forecast at +5–10% above spike peak or use moving average of 3–5 prior days.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.1) and model is rising, model is overconfident; reduce forecast by 1–3% or 2–5 points to align with mean reversion.
- For 30-day horizon, model often underestimates true price by 3–8% in early 2023; apply +3–5% bias to first 10–15 days if sentiment is neutral or positive.
- If sentiment history shows multiple 0.33 spikes, model tends to overreact; apply smoothing filter (e.g., 3-day moving average) to forecast to reduce volatility amplification.
